draft.title: Hypothetical reproducibility check: Model A vs. Model B
draft.body: I'm considering a hypothetical experiment to evaluate reproducibility in local LLMs. The scenario involves comparing two distinct local models, Model A and Model B. To ensure a fair and repeatable comparison, it's crucial to meticulously record all relevant parameters. This includes the specific model versions used, the exact prompt structure, all generation settings (like temperature, top-p, etc.), and the hardware configuration on which the tests would be run. Without this detailed information, any observed differences in output would be difficult to attribute reliably. This is purely a hypothetical setup; no actual results have been generated or observed. The core question is: what would be the best practice for documenting such a comparison to maximize the chances of others replicating the findings, assuming we were to conduct it?
draft.plan: This draft focuses on the hypothetical nature of the experiment and outlines the necessary documentation for reproducibility. It explicitly states that no results exist and frames the discussion around best practices for documentation in such a scenario. The goal is to solicit advice on how to set up the documentation framework for a future, hypothetical test.

draft.title: Designing a Hypothetical Reproducibility Study for Local LLMs
draft.body: Let's consider a hypothetical study designed to assess the reproducibility of outputs between two local language models. The premise is to isolate variables that influence model responses. To achieve this, a critical step would be to standardize and document every aspect of the testing environment and procedure. This includes specifying the exact model versions, the precise wording and structure of the input prompts, and all inference parameters such as temperature, top-k, and repetition penalties. Furthermore, the hardware specifications (CPU, GPU, RAM) must be recorded. This hypothetical experiment aims to establish a baseline for comparing the two models under identical conditions. It's important to emphasize that this is a conceptual exercise, and no actual experimental data or outcomes have been generated. The objective is to discuss the methodology for ensuring reproducibility in such a comparative setup.
draft.plan: This draft also emphasizes the hypothetical nature of the experiment. It focuses on the methodological aspects of designing a study to ensure reproducibility. By detailing the specific parameters that would need to be controlled and recorded, it sets the stage for a discussion on the best practices for setting up such a comparative test, explicitly stating that no results are available.
